psychoactives.name: Bog Myrtle (Myrica gale)
psychoactives.notes: Ancient Gaelic gruit ale herb; mild clarifying sedative/relaxant in tea or traditional ale. Legal to buy, forage, consume.

psychoactives.name: Heather (Calluna vulgaris)
psychoactives.notes: Used in fermented meads/ales by Highland tribes; subtle euphoric/relaxing herbal property in blooms.

spirits.name: Peated single malt Scotch
spirits.notes: Barley dried over peat fires — campfire, earth, ocean brine.

spirits.name: Heather ale
spirits.notes: Ancient ale style brewed with flowering heather instead of hops.

psychoactives.name: Bog Myrtle (Myrica gale)
psychoactives.notes: Shared Gaelic brewing tradition with Scotland; gruit ales.

spirits.name: Poitín
spirits.notes: Irish moonshine from malted barley/oats/potato; banned 1779, re-legalized 1997; 40–90%+ ABV.

psychoactives.name: Wild Lettuce (Lactuca virosa)
psychoactives.notes: Stem latex lactucarium ('lettuce opium') — mild legal sedative/relaxant; Roman Britain herbalism.

psychoactives.name: Valerian root (Valeriana officinalis)
psychoactives.notes: Legal tea/tincture hypnotic/sedative used since Greco-Roman times.

spirits.name: Scrumpy cider / perry
spirits.notes: Unpasteurized West Country apple/pear cider; often still; 8–9% ABV.

spirits.name: Navy strength gin
spirits.notes: ≥57% ABV; historic Royal Navy gunpowder test.

psychoactives.name: Grand wormwood (Artemisia absinthium)
psychoactives.notes: Thujone-bearing herb behind absinthe; dried herb and traditional spirits legal; raw oil extracts regulated.

spirits.name: Chartreuse
spirits.notes: Carthusian monks since 1737; ~130 alpine herbs; Green 55% ABV.

psychoactives.name: Cannabis social clubs
psychoactives.notes: Private non-commercial clubs (e.g. Barcelona, Basque) allow member/guest consumption inside club space — not street shops.

spirits.name: Patxaran
spirits.notes: Basque/Navarre sloe berry liqueur with coffee bean and cinnamon in anise spirit.

spirits.name: Orujo de Galicia
spirits.notes: Pomace brandy; often herb-infused (orujo de hierbas).

psychoactives.name: Decriminalization framework (2001)
psychoactives.notes: Personal possession of substances is an administrative matter, not a criminal offense — not the same as legal retail shops.

spirits.name: Aguardente de Medronho
spirits.notes: Algarve mountain spirit from strawberry-tree (medronho) fruit.

spirits.name: Ginjinha (Ginja)
spirits.notes: Lisbon/Óbidos sour-cherry liqueur in aguardente; often with a cherry in the glass.

spirits.name: Licor Beirão
spirits.notes: National sweet liqueur; secret blend of 13 plants/seeds including eucalyptus.

historical_caution: Henbane, mandrake, and deadly nightshade contain lethal tropane alkaloids and are not sold as recreational consumables.
